claim: The book calls discrete RVs 'the most realistic class' because the world/computers operate discretely, but drops the source's immediate caveat that continuous RVs and uncountable infinities are useful and tied to fundamental laws/approximations.
source_evidence: Transcript 1362.34-1377.98 calls the class realistic but says continuous RVs and uncountable infinity are very useful; 1382.12-1409.40 further qualifies the discrete-world intuition by discussing useful continuous approximations.
analysis: This does not create a false theorem, but removing the caveat makes an informal pedagogical claim more categorical and may incorrectly suggest continuous models are merely irrelevant or illegitimate. It is a genuine fidelity weakening the blind mathematical review did not inspect.
recommended_disposition: Restore a compact caveat after line 111: continuous models remain fundamental/useful despite finite digital representations.
